correctness.rationale: The finite domain has exactly 3^12 states and the twelve cube edges define the graph unambiguously. A vectorized complete functional graph, followed by exact indegree peeling and reverse-depth assignment, computes all orbits and basins; a separately coded C++ direct-trail classifier recreates the same counts without indegree peeling. Period, basin and depth histograms sum to all 531441 states. Their joint period table gives 18912 disagreements, CCA oscillatory population 18936, GHM 24, ratio 789. A separate 48-isometry times 3-color-cycle action verifies the CCA ten-class orbit decomposition. No infinite statement is extrapolated.

value.rationale: At the critical half-degree threshold on a canonical 12-vertex four-regular polyhedral graph, the choice between cyclic-contact and refractory updates changes the entire attractor landscape. New CCA periods 6, 8 and 12 are absent from GHM, the oscillation-attraction probability increases exactly 789-fold, and isolated short cycles coexist with attracting longer cycles. This exact natural finite classification supplies a reproducible boundary benchmark; its interest does not rely on claiming arbitrary-graph generality.
